_readme: Every entry requires source_url and as_of date. scope is 'company_specific' (verified specific to UP) or 'industry_typical' (used broadly across Class I railroads; not confirmed as UP's specific product, but generically accurate to name). Do not add an entry without a source. generate_rail_wiki.py may only reference systems by source_id.

domain_01_service_design.name: Unified Plan 2020
domain_01_service_design.detail: UP's own operating plan implementing Precision Scheduled Railroading principles, announced Sept 2018, rolled out in phases from Oct 1 2018. Included the 'Blend and Balance' train service concept, which UP itself later determined by mid-2018 was 'virtually impossible to execute reliably and consistently' in its original form and redesigned.

domain_01_service_design.name: NetControl (service design use)
domain_01_service_design.detail: Cross-referenced from RR-12/RR-02 — NetControl's business logic layer processes car trip plans and terminal missions that originate as service-design output. Primary system ownership sits in Technology (RR-12); this entry exists so RR-01 process pages can cite the same source_id rather than inventing a new name.

domain_02_dispatching.name: NetControl / CADx (Computer-Aided Dispatch)
domain_02_dispatching.detail: UP's dispatching platform since the Jan 6 2024 cutover, part of the same 'big three' modernization as PTC and transportation management. Replaced the legacy Transportation Control System (TCS).

domain_02_dispatching.name: Harriman Dispatching Center (HDC)
domain_02_dispatching.detail: UP's centralized dispatching facility in downtown Omaha, opened 1989, consolidating 10 regional dispatching centers into one location. Built inside a hardened former freight depot ('The Bunker').

domain_02_dispatching.name: Transportation Control System (TCS) — historical, retired
domain_02_dispatching.detail: UP's prior mainframe-based dispatching/transportation system, in service 50+ years, retired Jan 6 2024 in favor of NetControl. Retain in the wiki as historical context only — do not present as a current system.

domain_03_terminal_yard.name: Bailey Yard (North Platte, NE)
domain_03_terminal_yard.detail: UP's largest classification yard and the largest in the world by area: ~2,850 acres, ~8 miles long, 315 miles of track, 17 receiving/16 departure tracks, two humps (eastbound 34 ft, westbound ~20 ft), 114 bowl tracks (49 westbound/65 eastbound). Handles roughly 10,000-14,000 railcars and ~139 trains per 24 hours; sorts ~3,000 cars/day via the humps at up to 4 cars/minute.

domain_03_terminal_yard.name: Hump yard (generic classification technology)
domain_03_terminal_yard.detail: Standard industry technology: a graded mound over which cars are pushed and gravity-rolled onto sorting ('bowl') tracks according to destination, replacing manual flat switching for high-volume classification.

domain_04_crew_management.name: PS Technology (PST)
domain_04_crew_management.detail: PS Technology is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Union Pacific Railroad. It builds and sells crew management software (including the CrewPro product line) to Class I, transit, and short line railroads industry-wide.
domain_04_crew_management.note: Confirm current UP-internal crew calling platform name before citing PST/CrewPro as UP's own production system — sourcing here only supports 'UP owns PST, which sells crew management software industry-wide,' not 'UP runs CrewPro internally.' Treat those as two separate claims.

domain_04_crew_management.name: CrewPro
domain_04_crew_management.detail: Crew management/scheduling product line built by PS Technology. Handles scheduling by availability and seniority, rest-status tracking, and certification/qualification expiration tracking. Deployed across Class I and short line railroads generally.

domain_04_crew_management.name: HASTUS
domain_04_crew_management.detail: GIRO crew/roster scheduling platform. Confirmed North American deployments are passenger rail/transit (BART, CTA, LA Metro, WMATA); no public sourcing found for Class I freight use. Include only as a passenger-rail comparator, not as a freight-industry system.
domain_04_crew_management.caution: do not present as a freight Class I system without further sourcing

domain_04_crew_management.name: CloudMoyo Crew Management (CCM)
domain_04_crew_management.detail: Cloud-native SaaS crew scheduling product marketed to rail/transportation operators generally; handles seniority, qualifications, HOS, and union rules.

domain_04_crew_management.name: trackHOS-class HOS monitoring tools
domain_04_crew_management.detail: Generic reference to HOS tracking/compliance tooling referenced in trade coverage; use as a category description, not a specific vendor claim for UP.

domain_05_mechanical.name: Wayside defect detector network (hot bearing / wheel impact / acoustic)
domain_05_mechanical.detail: Standard industry category of trackside sensors that detect overheating bearings, wheel impact loads, and acoustic bearing defects as trains pass, without stopping the train.
domain_05_mechanical.caution: detector category is industry-standard; do not attribute a specific detector count or vendor to UP without further sourcing

domain_05_mechanical.name: Downing B. Jenks Shop (North Little Rock, AR)
domain_05_mechanical.detail: UP's largest locomotive shop and North America's foremost overhaul facility, performing all heavy locomotive maintenance on the railroad; employs 1,000+ people. In 2023 the team dismantled and rebuilt 200 units.

domain_05_mechanical.name: North Platte, NE locomotive shop
domain_05_mechanical.detail: UP's second-largest locomotive shop, historically employing ~600 people; distinct facility from Bailey Yard's classification operations at the same city.
domain_05_mechanical.as_of: historical reference — verify current staffing before citing a number

domain_05_mechanical.name: Proviso Locomotive Shop (Illinois)
domain_05_mechanical.detail: UP shop adjacent to the nation's largest rail hub (Chicago), maintaining the railroad's low-horsepower locomotive fleet used for yard/industry switching. Named in UP's own trade coverage of a winter-weather air-brake freezing issue (A-1 charging valve) that led to an operating-rule change for locomotive shutdown policy.

domain_05_mechanical.name: West Colton Yard and Shops (Colton, CA)
domain_05_mechanical.detail: UP heavy maintenance facility where locomotive repainting and related shop work occurs.

domain_05_mechanical.name: Wabtec Modular Control Architecture (AC4400 modernization program)
domain_05_mechanical.detail: UP signed a $1.2 billion agreement with Wabtec to modernize its AC4400 locomotive fleet with updated propulsion, control, and diagnostics systems built on Wabtec's Modular Control Architecture — a standardized computing/software platform enabling condition-based maintenance (real-time fault/performance reporting) rather than strictly time-based service intervals. Program targets an 80% reliability improvement and a 14% increase in tractive effort.

domain_05_mechanical.name: NEXSYS III-i microprocessor locomotive control system
domain_05_mechanical.detail: Named as the onboard control system on specific UP locomotive units (GP38N/GP39N) in a locomotive roster reference — advanced control options, increased adhesion, integrated AESS (auto engine start-stop) technology.
domain_05_mechanical.caution: sourced from a locomotive-roster/enthusiast site rather than a UP primary source; treat as company-specific to these unit classes but verify before citing broadly

domain_06_engineering.name: I-ETMS (Interoperable Electronic Train Management System)
domain_06_engineering.detail: Union Pacific is one of the four original railroads (with BNSF, CSX, Norfolk Southern) that developed and jointly submitted the I-ETMS PTC Development Plan to FRA. UP's PTC implementation is built on I-ETMS, supplied by Wabtec.

domain_06_engineering.name: Wabtrax
domain_06_engineering.detail: Wabtec's track database creation/validation tool used by 'all Class I railroads' to build and validate PTC track databases (the subdivision track data files). Named as an industry-wide tool, not confirmed UP-exclusive branding.

domain_06_engineering.name: PTC Back Office Server (BOS)
domain_06_engineering.detail: Wabtec's PTC BOS product is explicitly named with Union Pacific among its Class I customer list, interfacing with existing dispatch office systems.

domain_06_engineering.name: NetControl
domain_06_engineering.detail: UP's transportation management platform, cut over 6 Jan 2024, replacing the 50+ year old mainframe Transportation Control System (TCS). Relevant to Engineering where subdivision/track asset data feeds train movement authority — but NetControl itself is a Dispatching/IT-domain system, cross-referenced here, not owned by Engineering.

domain_06_engineering.name: FRA Automated Track Inspection Program (ATIP)
domain_06_engineering.detail: IMPORTANT NAMING CAVEAT: ATIP is the Federal Railroad Administration's OWN fleet of track inspection cars, conducting compliance surveys of 50,000-100,000 miles/year. It is a government program, not a UP-branded system. CN separately uses the same acronym ('Autonomous Track Inspection Program') for its own branded fleet. No public sourcing found for UP using the name 'ATIP' for its internal program.

domain_06_engineering.name: UP automated/autonomous track inspection program (unbranded)
domain_06_engineering.detail: UP operates a crewed Hi-Rail system, one crewed traditional track geometry car, ten automated locomotive-mounted systems, and three boxcar-mounted autonomous systems. Program began approximately 2019; UP reports defects down ~85% over five years. No confirmed public brand name for this program as of last research — refer to it descriptively, not as 'ATIP.'

domain_06_engineering.name: Track geometry car (generic)
domain_06_engineering.detail: Standard industry category: rail-mounted vehicle measuring gauge, curvature, alignment, cross-level, surface smoothness without obstructing operations. Generic term, not a product name.

domain_06_engineering.name: RailAI (Tetra Tech)
domain_06_engineering.detail: Autonomous unmanned track inspection railcar product, operating in revenue service with unnamed North American Class I railroads and under FRA's ATIP. Not confirmed as a UP-specific deployment.

domain_07_safety_regulatory.name: GCOR (General Code of Operating Rules)
domain_07_safety_regulatory.detail: UP publishes and applies its own GCOR-based rule book (up.com/ert/gcor.pdf). GCOR is used by Class I railroads west of Chicago, most Class II railroads, and many short lines; railroads east of Chicago generally use NORAC instead. Currently in a 9th edition (effective Sept 23 2026 per trade summary) superseding prior editions; UP has historically issued its own amendments/special instructions on top of the base code.

domain_07_safety_regulatory.name: C3RS (Confidential Close Call Reporting System)
domain_07_safety_regulatory.detail: FRA-sponsored voluntary confidential close-call reporting program used across the rail industry, modeled on aviation ASRS-style non-punitive reporting. Named generically here pending confirmation of UP's specific participation status.
domain_07_safety_regulatory.caution: confirm UP's specific enrollment/site status before presenting as company-specific

domain_08_hazmat_environmental.name: AskRail
domain_08_hazmat_environmental.detail: Free mobile app giving vetted first responders real-time hazmat/railcar contents data during a rail incident. Launched Oct 2014 as a joint effort of all North American Class I railroads, Amtrak, the International Association of Fire Chiefs, AAR, and Railinc (which administers it). Serves 2.3M+ registered first responders across 49 states, DC, and 8 Canadian provinces. Not UP-specific — a shared industry utility.

domain_08_hazmat_environmental.name: TRANSCAER (Transportation Community Awareness and Emergency Response)
domain_08_hazmat_environmental.detail: Voluntary national outreach program founded in 1986 by Union Pacific and Dow Chemical Company, focused on helping communities prepare for and respond to hazmat transportation incidents. UP is a founding organization, though the program is now industry-wide.

domain_08_hazmat_environmental.name: SERTC (Security and Emergency Response Training Center)
domain_08_hazmat_environmental.detail: Rail industry's shared hazmat emergency-response training facility, located in Pueblo, Colorado; trains thousands of first responders annually.

domain_09_intermodal_automotive.name: UPGo
domain_09_intermodal_automotive.detail: UP's mobile app for truck drivers at intermodal ramps, built on driver feedback data. Used alongside machine-vision no-stop gate technology to reduce wait times; UP used gate-technology data from its Global IV Intermodal Terminal (Chicago area) to work with beneficial cargo owners (BCOs) on optimal container pull times.

domain_09_intermodal_automotive.name: EMP and UMAX container fleets
domain_09_intermodal_automotive.detail: UP-branded nationwide domestic intermodal container fleets, named on UP's own intermodal customer page.

domain_09_intermodal_automotive.name: Driver scanning / gate technology (generic 'Yard System')
domain_09_intermodal_automotive.detail: UP describes an 'advanced Yard System that coordinates all movement of rail cars, trucks, trailers and containers' at its intermodal terminals, plus GPS-guided cranes and driver-scanning gate technology cutting truck processing time from several minutes to as little as 30-90 seconds. Named generically across multiple UP terminal openings (Dallas, Joliet); not a single confirmed product name.

domain_09_intermodal_automotive.name: ICTF (Intermodal Container Transfer Facility), Long Beach
domain_09_intermodal_automotive.detail: UP-operated near-dock rail yard serving the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach; installed the industry's first hybrid electric crane there to reduce emissions. ~250 acres, on-site storage for 3,000+ containers.

domain_09_intermodal_automotive.name: Joliet Intermodal Terminal
domain_09_intermodal_automotive.detail: 785-acre UP intermodal terminal in Joliet, Illinois, opened to handle international shipment growth to/from Chicago and connections to eastern Class I and short line railroads.

domain_09_intermodal_automotive.name: Global IV Intermodal Terminal (Chicago area)
domain_09_intermodal_automotive.detail: Named UP intermodal terminal outside Chicago where draymen/BCO wait-time issues were diagnosed and addressed using gate-technology data.

domain_10_commercial.name: Loup Logistics
domain_10_commercial.detail: Wholly-owned Union Pacific subsidiary, launched Nov 1 2017 as the merger of four prior UP subsidiaries: Union Pacific Distribution Services (UPDS), Streamline, ShipCarsNow, and Insight Network Logistics (INL). Provides door-to-door shipping/logistics, transload distribution ('One Plus' pricing bundling rail, transload, and truck), and wind-component chain-of-custody services.

domain_10_commercial.name: ShipmentVision
domain_10_commercial.detail: Loup Logistics' shipment tracking/visibility platform — 24/7 track-and-trace across all rail carriers and modes, customizable dashboards, dynamic ETAs, transit time calculator. Available only to Loup customers.

domain_10_commercial.name: UP customer portal (up.com secure portal)
domain_10_commercial.detail: UP's own site describes a 'secure customer portal to plan, ship, track and pay for your shipments,' plus EDI (computer-to-computer document exchange) and cloud-storage sync. No specific product/brand name confirmed beyond this generic description on up.com.
domain_10_commercial.caution: confirm actual product name (if one exists) before citing more specifically than 'UP's customer portal'

domain_10_commercial.name: Transentric — historical, verify current status
domain_10_commercial.detail: Named in a 2004 case study as UP's 'software subsidiary,' working with UPDS (Loup's predecessor). This is a 20+ year old reference — do not present as current without verifying Transentric still exists or was absorbed elsewhere.
domain_10_commercial.caution: do not present as a current system without re-verification

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: Umler (Universal Machine Language Equipment Register)
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: The industry's centralized electronic equipment registry, managed by Railinc for the AAR. Registers over 2 million pieces of equipment (railcars, locomotives, trailers, containers, chassis, end-of-train devices) with physical characteristics, ownership, and pool assignment data. Authoritative source for interchange eligibility under AAR Interchange Rules 90 and 93; feeds CHARM (Car Hire Accounting Rate Master) and TRAIN II. Established 1968, originally on punch cards.

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: CHARM (Car Hire Accounting Rate Master)
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: Industry file verified against Umler that determines car hire billing rates for equipment in interchange service.

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: TRAIN II (Tele Rail Automated Information Network Phase 2)
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: The rail industry's national car information/tracking system, verified against the Umler master file.

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: EHMS (Equipment Health Management System)
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: Railinc-operated system tracking equipment health/defect data, part of the same Railinc product suite as Umler and DDCT (Damaged and Defective Car Tracking).

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: Interline Settlement System (ISS) / Switching Settlement Data Exchange (SSDX) / Car Hire Data Exchange (CHDX)
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: AAR Railway Accounting Rules (RAR)-governed systems for waybilling and settlement of interline shipments.

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: Ferromex (FXE) interchange — Eagle Pass gateway
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: UP's #2 U.S.-Mexico rail gateway by volume (behind CPKC's Laredo-Nuevo Laredo crossing). As of Nov 20 2025, UP shifted the FXE interchange point from the International Railway Bridge itself to UP's Clark Park Yard, 7 rail miles from the border, using Mexican partner crews qualified/certified by UP to bring trains to the yard before a U.S. crew change — cutting bridge transit time by 50% and implemented under CBP's Secure Corridor Initiative.

domain_11_interline_equipment.name: UP Mexico gateway network
domain_11_interline_equipment.detail: UP states its Mexico gateway coverage is the broadest and most direct of any US Class I. Named gateways for at least LPG/petroleum products: Calexico, El Paso, Nogales, Eagle Pass, Laredo, Brownsville. UP connects with Mexican railroads FXE (Ferromex) and KCSM (now part of CPKC de Mexico).
domain_11_interline_equipment.caution: Laredo-Nuevo Laredo is controlled by CPKC, not UP, per separate sourcing — UP's own gateway page lists Laredo among product-specific routes but the primary Laredo rail bridge is a CPKC asset; verify UP's actual interchange arrangement at Laredo before writing a specific process there.

domain_12_technology.name: NetControl
domain_12_technology.detail: UP's transportation management platform (primary domain owner). Built on a service-oriented architecture; intakes millions of messages/day from customers, other railroads, and internal systems; applies business logic driving 75 key internal/external reporting measures; can trace every car on the network. Development took ~10 years and was described in trade coverage as costing approximately $200 million; cutover completed within roughly 3 hours on Jan 6 2024.

domain_12_technology.name: PS Technology (PST)
domain_12_technology.detail: Wholly-owned UP subsidiary building rail-industry software (crew management via CrewPro among other product lines), sold to Class I, transit, and short line customers industry-wide. Cross-referenced from RR-04.

domain_12_technology.name: Physics Train Builder
domain_12_technology.detail: PRIMARY SOURCE — named directly in UP's FY2025 Form 10-K (SEC filing). Proprietary UP technology evaluating train and route characteristics to enable proactive derailment-prevention intervention by the Operating Practices Command Center.

domain_12_technology.name: Operating Practices Command Center
domain_12_technology.detail: PRIMARY SOURCE — named in UP's FY2025 10-K as the operational team that acts on Physics Train Builder outputs to intervene proactively and prevent derailments.

domain_12_technology.name: COMMIT (Situational Awareness Testing program)
domain_12_technology.detail: PRIMARY SOURCE — named in UP's FY2025 10-K. Program that observes, tests, and coaches employees to promote understanding of and compliance with work rules, with emphasis on in-the-field training. Cross-references RR-07 efficiency testing.

domain_12_technology.name: Machine Vision portals
domain_12_technology.detail: UP-deployed trackside video-analytics/machine-learning inspection portals. As of a 2018 trade interview with then-CIO Lynden Tennison, UP had no immediate plans to expand further but noted a theoretical network-wide maximum of ~70 portals if deployed on all high-traffic mainlines. Verify current deployment count before citing as a present-day figure — this is an 8-year-old data point.
domain_12_technology.caution: figure is dated; re-verify before presenting as current

domain_12_technology.name: Cybersecurity — 'secure-by-design' approach (unbranded)
domain_12_technology.detail: Current CIO Rahul Jalali describes UP's cybersecurity posture as 'secure-by-design,' with industry-wide collaboration on threat-sharing rather than competing on safety/cyber risk; named future direction includes zero-trust cybersecurity. No specific platform/vendor name sourced — do not invent one.

domain_13_finance.name: Fuel surcharge program
domain_13_finance.detail: UP's mechanism for recovering fuel cost exposure from customers, disclosed in every UP 10-K/10-Q. Per UP's own risk disclosure, fuel surcharge programs trail fluctuations in fuel price by approximately two months, creating a real quarter-over-quarter revenue volatility source. Distinct from index-based contract escalators (formulas correlating price adjustments to economic indices), which also contain some fuel provision but are accounted for separately.
domain_13_finance.as_of: 2015 disclosure language (mechanism description is stable across UP's 10-K history)

domain_13_finance.name: ARC (Average Revenue per Car)
domain_13_finance.detail: UP's core disclosed freight-revenue metric. Freight revenues vary with volume (carloads) and ARC; ARC itself is driven by price changes, traffic mix, and fuel surcharges. Reported every quarter in UP's 10-Q/10-K filings.

domain_14_hr_labor.name: TE&Y (Train, Engine & Yard) New Hire Training program
domain_14_hr_labor.detail: UP's redesigned new-hire training program: an 8-week 'sandbox' environment using actual equipment (locomotives, rail cars, track, switches) under instructor supervision, ~85% field time. Replaced an older process that took 18 weeks and heavily emphasized classroom theory. Recognized as a Training Top 100 Best Practice.

domain_14_hr_labor.name: Mobile classroom training trailers
domain_14_hr_labor.detail: Fleet of 5 mobile classrooms UP built (as of 2012) to bring operations/safety training and locomotive simulators to engineer and conductor locations across its 23-state system. Each has 7 workstations (2 employees each) with simulator webcams enabling remote instructors based in Salt Lake City, Utah and Omaha, Nebraska to assist students.

domain_15_merger_integration.name: NetControl / TCS cutover precedent
domain_15_merger_integration.detail: UP's own recent experience (Jan 2024) migrating all core operating systems in a single cutover is a genuine, citable internal precedent for the systems-integration risk discussion in a merger context — distinct from, and not to be confused with, the systems consolidation that would be required to integrate with Norfolk Southern's systems.
